commits.author: Marco Andronaco
commits.subject: fix: keep live updates working for sessions the event stream doesn't cover
commits.body:
Two independent gaps let the UI sit indefinitely on stale data while
reporting a healthy connection.

Poll fallback: "connected" only proves the SSE stream is open, not that it
carries a given session. opencode emits events on an in-process bus, so a
session driven by a different opencode process (a local TUI running its own
server) produces no events here even though the stream is fine, and f417e3e
suppressed the poll for exactly that case. Track the last event seen per
session and skip the poll only while the open session is actually receiving
events, so the redundant refetch during active streaming stays gone while
uncovered sessions fall back to polling.

Stream watchdog: the read loop awaited reader.read() with no timeout. A
connection that dies silently (sleep/resume, NAT or proxy timeout) never
rejects the pending read and never delivers done, so the stream stayed in
"connected" forever and suppressed the fallback with it. Arm a watchdog
around each read, defaulting to 30s against the server's 10s heartbeat, and
abort plus cancel the reader on expiry so the existing reconnect path runs.
Cancelling matters because aborting does not reliably propagate into the
body stream.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix(bridge): beat on the event stream so clients do not reconnect on a loop
commits.body:
#37 added a stall watchdog to the SSE transport that aborts and reconnects when
no bytes arrive for 30s, since a TCP stream can die without ever erroring. The
premise holds for OpenCode, which beats every 10s, but the bridge only wrote
when a session event occurred, so an idle OMP session looked like a dead
connection: measured in the browser, the stream was torn down and re-established
at 31s and 62s, indefinitely. With a heartbeat the same window holds a single
connection.

That churn also suppressed the polling fallback, which #37 skips while live
updates report connected, leaving a gap where neither was running.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: docs: add a contributing guide
commits.body:
The repo expects seven web checks plus the bridge suite, its regression tests
assert against source text rather than rendering, and a change has to hold on
every backend or it surfaces a 404 to the user. None of that was written down,
so #36 had to inline the commands and a newcomer had to infer the rest.
